provenance.note: Starter pack authored from general machine-design practice; application-specific values must come from revision-bound sources.

terminology.definition: The clamp force established in a bolted joint by tightening, before external service load is applied.
An empirical dimensionless coefficient lumping thread and underhead friction and geometry into the torque-preload relation T = K F d. It is condition-specific, not a material constant.

provenance.citation: Bickford, An Introduction to the Design and Behavior of Bolted Joints
provenance.note: The exact K value must come from the joint's test or a qualified source, not from a default.

terminology.definition: The effective thread cross-section used to convert bolt axial force to nominal tensile stress.

provenance.note: The model is a closed-form scalar relation; uncertainty in K is propagated explicitly.

provenance.citation: ASME B1.1 Unified Inch Screw Threads
provenance.note: Metadata only; use the licensed standard text for authoritative clauses.

assumptions.statement: Thread friction, underhead friction and thread geometry are lumped into the single condition-specific nut factor K.

provenance.citation: Bickford, An Introduction to the Design and Behavior of Bolted Joints
provenance.note: Lubricant, coating, surface finish and re-use must match the K source.

assumptions.statement: Tightening is quasi-static and the reported torque is the torque actually delivered to the fastener.

provenance.note: Dynamic torque, tool losses and torque-rate effects must be measured, not assumed.

assumptions.statement: Embedment, creep and relaxation after tightening are not modeled unless a separate time-dependent analysis is supplied.

provenance.note: Missing relaxation data remains unknown; it is not zero.

validity_domains.statement: The nut factor K is valid only inside the range established by the exact joint condition and test source. K outside that range invalidates the preload result.
exclusions: re-used fasteners outside the qualified condition

validity_domains.statement: The stress conversion is a nominal elastic estimate; yielding, thread stripping and local plasticity require a different model.

property_sources.authority: Manufacturer datasheet plus ISO 898-1 property class, revision-bound

provenance.note: Minimum proof strength is not inferred from a generic material name.

property_sources.authority: Joint-specific torque/clamp-force test or qualified supplier data, revision-bound
Controlled drawing or licensed thread standard, revision-bound

provenance.citation: ASME B1.1 Unified Inch Screw Threads

design_rules.rule: Compare the calculated nominal bolt stress with the revision-bound proof strength and report utilization.

provenance.note: The allowable utilization is an explicit design decision.

design_rules.rule: Never use a default K without a condition-specific provenance and validity range.
design_rules.check: K source revision and validity range are present

provenance.citation: Bickford, An Introduction to the Design and Behavior of Bolted Joints

design_rules.rule: Account for torque-tool calibration and delivered-torque uncertainty separately from K scatter.
design_rules.check: torque uncertainty has a calibration provenance

manufacturing_rules.rule: Control and record lubricant, coating, thread condition and washer condition because they change K.
manufacturing_rules.check: assembly record matches the K test condition

manufacturing_rules.rule: Use calibrated torque equipment and lot-traceable fasteners for safety-relevant joints.
manufacturing_rules.check: tool calibration and fastener lot are recorded

failure_modes.mode: bolt overload or yield during tightening
failure_modes.cause: torque too high for the actual K, thread friction lower than assumed, or proof strength lower than assumed
failure_modes.detection: preload measurement, torque-angle signature, dimensional inspection after yield

failure_modes.mode: insufficient clamp force, loosening or fatigue
failure_modes.cause: torque too low, high friction, embedment or relaxation
failure_modes.detection: preload audit, vibration test, joint movement inspection

diagnostic_signatures.signature: preload scatter far wider than torque-tool uncertainty
diagnostic_signatures.indicates: K variation from friction, lubrication or thread condition; do not average it away

test_methods.method: Torque/clamp-force test with the production joint condition
test_methods.measures: K distribution, clamp force, friction condition

standards_mappings.scope: systematic calculation of high-duty bolted joints

worked_cases.description: A 12 mm bolt tightened to 100 N*m with K = 0.2 produces a clamp force from T/(K d).

inputs.name: nut_factor
inputs.note: condition-specific value supplied by the case

expected.name: preload
expected.note: T/(K d), no stress-area assumption involved

provenance.citation: Closed-form evaluation of T = K F d
provenance.note: The numeric value follows from the equation and the supplied inputs; it is not a property claim.

counterexamples.claim: A torque value fixes preload independently of friction.
counterexamples.refutation: T = K F d makes preload inversely proportional to K. Doubling K halves preload for the same torque; K must be measured for the actual joint condition.

known_traps.trap: Using an unrealistically low K (for example 0.02) in T = K F d to obtain a dramatic preload.
known_traps.why_shallow_fails: The arithmetic looks correct, but the result is outside the validity of any realistic joint condition and implies an impossible friction state.
known_traps.guard: Require a K validity range with provenance; refuse the analysis when the supplied K lies outside it.
